record.original_question: Let p be a prime. Let G be a transitive subgroup of the group of finitary permutations F Sym(Ω) of a set Ω, let N be a normal subgroup of G, and let S be a transitive Sylow p-subgroup of G. (a) Is it true that S ∩ N is a Sylow p-subgroup of N? (b) Is it true that SN/N is a Sylow p-subgroup of G/N? (c) Are any two transitive Sylow p-subgroups of G locally conjugate in G? Two subgroups X, Y of a group G are said to be locally conjugate if there is a locally inner automorphism φ of G such that X φ = Y. An automorphism φ of G is said to be locally inner if for every finite subset A ⊆ G there is an element g = g(A) ∈ G such that aφ = g −1 ag for all a ∈ A.

artifact.category_tag: Sylow theory in finitary symmetric groups
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $p$ be a prime and let $\Omega$ be a (possibly infinite) set. Denote by $\mathrm{FSym}(\Omega)$ the group of all finitary permutations of $\Omega$, i.e. permutations of $\Omega$ moving only finitely many points. A subgroup $H \le \mathrm{FSym}(\Omega)$ is called transitive if it acts transitively on $\Omega$. A Sylow $p$-subgroup of a group is a maximal $p$-subgroup.

For a group $G$, an automorphism $\varphi$ of $G$ is called locally inner if for every finite subset $A \subseteq G$ there exists $g = g(A) \in G$ such that $a^{\varphi} = g^{-1} a g$ for all $a \in A$. Two subgroups $X, Y \le G$ are called locally conjugate in $G$ if there exists a locally inner automorphism $\varphi$ of $G$ with $X^{\varphi} = Y$.

Let $G \le \mathrm{FSym}(\Omega)$ be a transitive subgroup, let $N \trianglelefteq G$ be a normal subgroup, and let $S$ be a transitive Sylow $p$-subgroup of $G$. Determine whether each of the following holds:

(a) Is $S \cap N$ a Sylow $p$-subgroup of $N$?

(b) Is $SN/N$ a Sylow $p$-subgroup of $G/N$?

(c) Are any two transitive Sylow $p$-subgroups of $G$ locally conjugate in $G$?
